002_h1: Food Revolution for Social Change with KULNA Garden
003_p: A four-year, federally funded action research project asking how individual and collective wellbeing shift when you change a food system. The question was never only about food.

017_figcaption: Harvest day at KULNA Community Garden, Zayed University, Dubai.
018_p: It started as a three-raised-bed experiment and became a small forest ecosystem on the campus.
019_p: “Co-designing Food Revolution for Social Change” was a four-year, federally funded action research project at Zayed University, asking how individual and collective wellbeing shift when you change a food system. The question was never only about food.
024_p: in Arabic. A physical sanctuary where students and faculty grew food, and in growing it, found reasons to be in the same place at the same time. Around the garden grew hands-on workshops, lectures, campaigns, and the ordinary interactions that turn a site into a community.
025_p: What emerged was a web of connection none of the participants could have seen alone — farmers, filmmakers, naturalists, permaculture researchers, students, volunteers — and, hidden inside it, a picture of what the future would ask of them.
026_p: The project produced multiple academic papers.
027_span: It also produced a network that is still exchanging today, long after the funding ended.
034_h2: Every practice began as one conversation.
